title: Family dispute not yet known to be family: the section cannot be fixed

expect.why: Article 423 lists what the family section hears and 426 gives its own territorial rules (marital home, domicile of the defendant, place of custody...). Which rule applies depends on whether the dispute is a family matter, which the case leaves unknown, so the rule must ask.

title: Wages claim: employment relation unknown, so social section and article 501 rule cannot be chosen

expect.why: Article 500 gives the social section exclusive jurisdiction in disputes on performance, suspension and ending of work contracts; article 501 then gives place of the contract, of its performance, or the defendant's domicile. Whether the dispute is social is left unknown, so the rule must ask.

title: Work contract ended: whether a work accident or occupational illness caused it is unknown

expect.why: Article 501 ¶1 gives place of conclusion or performance of the contract or the defendant's domicile; ¶2 (and article 40 item 8) gives the plaintiff's domicile when the contract ends or is suspended by a work accident or occupational illness. The two paragraphs lead to different courts and the fact that selects one is unknown, so the rule must ask.

title: Social dispute in a court with no social section

expect.why: Article 32 ¶5: where sections are not created the civil section hears all disputes 'باستثناء القضايا الاجتماعية'. The text excludes social cases from the civil section but does not say which section hears them in such a court. The text does not settle this; the rule must warn, not decide.

title: Family matter: whether the court has a family section is unknown

expect.why: Article 32 ¶5: where sections are not created the civil section hears all disputes except social ones, so a family case goes to the civil section in a court without a family section (¶6 refers a misfiled case to the right section). Whether the section exists is unknown, so the rule must ask.

title: Employer in judicial settlement, wages claim: article 40 item 3 against article 501

expect.why: Article 40 ¶4 sends bankruptcy or judicial settlement of companies to the court where it was opened or the registered office; ¶9 and article 501 send labour disputes to the place of contract, performance or defendant's domicile, all 'دون سواها'. The text does not say which governs a wage claim against a company in settlement. The text does not settle this; the rule must warn.

title: Jurisdiction clause in a contract: whether the parties are merchants is unknown

expect.why: Article 45: a clause giving territorial jurisdiction to a court that is not competent is void, 'إلا إذا تم بين التجار'. Whether the clause is valid depends on whether the parties are merchants, which is unknown, so the rule must ask.

title: Commercial dispute where only one party is a merchant: clause exception unclear

expect.why: The slot is yes for a dispute between merchants or about a commercial act. Article 45 saves the clause only if made 'بين التجار'; a commercial act between a merchant and a non-merchant is not clearly 'between merchants'. The text does not settle this; the rule must warn, not decide.

title: Partition of an estate that includes real property: place of the property or domicile of the deceased

expect.why: Article 40 ¶2 item 1 gives real-property matters to the court of the property; ¶3 item 2 gives inheritance matters to the court of the deceased's domicile, both 'دون سواها'. The text does not say which governs the partition of an estate containing real property. The text does not settle this; the rule must warn.

title: Lease of business premises: is it real property for article 40 item 1?

expect.why: Article 40 ¶2 names 'دعاوى الإيجارات بما فيها التجارية المتعلقة بالعقارات', so the court of the property is the only court; article 39 item 4 (commercial matters) is the alternative for other commercial disputes. The slot on real property is unknown and its wording does not name a commercial lease, so the rule must ask.

title: Defendant lives abroad: no domicile in the territory

expect.why: Article 37: the court of the defendant's domicile, or, if none is known, of his last domicile, or the chosen domicile. The text does not say what applies to a defendant whose domicile or last domicile is outside the national territory. The text does not settle this; the rule must warn.
